name: Predator
what_it_is: Open-source platform for managing the full lifecycle of API load testing, from authoring and scheduling tests to distributed execution and real-time reporting. Built on Artillery as its load-test engine and deployable on Kubernetes, DC/OS, or Docker.
components: Kafka streaming integration for resource production
measurement: Concurrent run aggregation across multiple runners
configuration: Cron expression scheduling for recurring test runs
Distributed load generation across unlimited runner instances
Webhooks: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord, generic JSON
fault_injection: Kubernetes Chaos Mesh integration to inject faults and failures into the target environment during load tests (introduced v1.7.0)
constraints: Predator-Runner Docker image version MUST match the manager's major.minor version — mismatches cause failures
Only tagged Docker image releases are supported; 'latest' tag is explicitly unsupported
Cassandra database support was dropped in v1.5.0 — only PostgreSQL, MySQL, MSSQL, SQLite are supported
Chaos Mesh fault injection requires a Kubernetes deployment; not available on plain Docker or DC/OS
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml found in master or main branches (404)
No documented support for gRPC, WebSockets, or non-HTTP protocols
No explicit concurrency or test-duration hard limits documented
No built-in authentication mechanism details documented
Specific Artillery assertion types available through functional mode are not enumerated in the README
